section: Juvenile Justice Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment 2016
subsections: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate

accepted.s: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, a ‘child’ means a person who has not completed which age?
o: 14 years
16 years
18 years
21 years
accepted.x: Under POCSO, a child is any person below 18 years of age.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory age threshold directly.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the gender applicability of the POCSO Act?
o: It applies only where the child and offender belong to different genders.
It protects only female children and applies only to male offenders.
It protects only children below 16 years and applies to offenders of either sex.
It is gender-neutral with respect to both the child and the offender.
accepted.x: The POCSO Act is gender-neutral in relation to both the child victim and the offender.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between gender-specific and gender-neutral statutory protection.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding consent under the POCSO Act:
1. Consent of a person below 18 years is legally irrelevant under the Act.
2. Sexual activity with a person below 18 may constitute statutory rape even where apparent consent is present.
3. The Act treats the age of consent as 16 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because POCSO fixes the relevant age at 18 years.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the statutory age against the debated age of consent.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence specifically identified under the POCSO Act?
o: Penetrative sexual assault
Child pornography
Sexual harassment of a child
Child marriage as an independent POCSO offence
accepted.x: POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography. Child marriage is not listed as an independent POCSO offence in this classification.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list of offences.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 19 of the POCSO Act, information about an offence is required to be reported to the:
o: District Child Welfare Committee only
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights only
Sessions Court directly
Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police
accepted.x: Section 19 requires information about a POCSO offence to be reported to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority responsible for receiving mandatory reports.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to mandatory reporting under the POCSO Act, consider the following statements:
1. Any person who knows of an offence is required to report it.
2. A child may also be required to report information about an offence.
3. Failure to report may attract imprisonment up to six months or a fine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Section 19 covers any person, including a child, and non-reporting may result in imprisonment up to six months or a fine.
accepted.tq: Check the reporting duty, its inclusive coverage and its penalty together.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the child-friendly procedure prescribed under the POCSO Act?
o: The statement should preferably be recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank who is not in uniform.
The child’s statement may be recorded at the child’s residence.
The statement may be recorded at a place chosen by the child.
The child must be questioned at the police station during the night to prevent interference.
accepted.x: A child must not be kept at a police station at night. The statement is preferably recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank, not in uniform, at the child’s residence or chosen place.
accepted.tq: Locate the reversed child-friendly safeguard.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I — Provision
 a. Section 19
 b. Sections 29–30
 c. Section 22

List-II — Subject
 i. False complaints
 ii. Mandatory reporting
 iii. Burden of proof on the accused
o: a–i, b–ii, c–iii
a–ii, b–iii, c–i
a–iii, b–i, c–ii
a–ii, b–i, c–iii
accepted.x: Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting, Sections 29–30 place the burden of proof on the accused, and Section 22 deals with false complaints, subject to the good-faith exception.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure statutory-section pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A false complaint under the POCSO Act is punishable, subject to an exception for complaints made:
o: before a Special Court בלבד
by a parent בלבד
in good faith
within one month of the alleged offence
accepted.x: False complaints are punishable under Section 22, but complaints made in good faith are excepted.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the statutory exception from restrictions not prescribed by the Act.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trial framework under the POCSO Act?
o: Trial before the High Court within one month without compensation provisions
In-camera trial, with investigation targeted within two months and trial within one year
Open trial within two years after investigation by any police station
Trial only before a Juvenile Justice Board within six months
accepted.x: POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.
accepted.tq: Combine the court type and statutory time limits without reversing them.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act, a person storing child pornographic material without deleting or reporting it may face a minimum fine of:
o: ₹1,000, increased to ₹2,000 for a repeat offence
₹5,000, increased to ₹10,000 for a repeat offence
₹20,000, with no enhanced repeat-offence amount
₹10,000, increased to ₹20,000 for a repeat offence
accepted.x: The minimum fine is ₹5,000 for storing child pornographic material, rising to ₹10,000 for a repeat offence.
accepted.tq: Separate the initial and repeat-offence monetary figures carefully.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which additional conduct was specifically addressed by the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: Failure to attend school up to 14 years
Employing a child in all forms of domestic work
Giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity
Permitting marriage below the statutory age
accepted.x: The 2019 amendment introduced punishment for giving chemicals to a child to hasten sexual maturity.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific conduct added by the amendment instead of a related child-protection offence.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages in the history of the age of consent in India in chronological order:
A. Age of Consent Act fixed the age at 12 years
B. IPC amendment fixed the age at 14 years
C. POCSO fixed the age at 18 years
D. IPC 1860 fixed the age at 10 years
o: D, A, B, C
A, D, B, C
D, B, A, C
B, A, D, C
accepted.x: The sequence is IPC 1860—10 years, Age of Consent Act 1891—12 years, IPC amendment 1925—14 years, and POCSO 2012—18 years.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest IPC provision and the final POCSO provision.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the progression of the age of consent mentioned in the legal framework?
o: 10 years in 1860, 14 in 1891, 16 in 1925, 18 in 1949 and 21 under POCSO 2012
10 years in 1860, 12 in 1891, 14 in 1925, 16 in 1949 and 18 under POCSO 2012
10 years in 1860, 12 in 1891, 16 in 1925, 18 in 1949 and 21 under POCSO 2012
12 years in 1860, 14 in 1891, 16 in 1925, 18 in 1949 and 21 under POCSO 2012
accepted.x: The progression is 10 years under IPC 1860, 12 under the 1891 Act, 14 after the 1925 amendment, 16 in 1949 and 18 under POCSO 2012.
accepted.tq: Compare the entire numerical sequence rather than checking only its final value.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Justice Verma Committee recommended reducing the age of consent to 16 years.
2. The 240th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development, 2011, rejected the concept of minor consent.
3. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retains 18 years as the age of consent under Section 63.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Justice Verma Committee supported 16 years, the 2011 parliamentary report rejected minor consent, and BNS Section 63 retains 18 years.
accepted.tq: Check recommendations and the current statutory position separately before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Madhya Pradesh High Court asked the Union Government to consider lowering the age of consent to 16 years primarily on the ground of:
o: early puberty associated with exposure through social media
the introduction of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
the difference between the age of marriage and voting age
declining school enrolment among adolescents
accepted.x: The Madhya Pradesh High Court cited early puberty linked to social-media exposure while asking the Centre to consider lowering the age of consent to 16 years.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial observation with its stated rationale.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the Supreme Court’s recent consideration of consensual adolescent relationships under POCSO?
o: It declared that Article 142 cannot be used in POCSO matters.
It removed the age threshold of 18 years from POCSO.
It urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause and flagged misuse in consensual adolescent relationships.
It transferred all POCSO trials to Juvenile Justice Boards.
accepted.x: In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court flagged misuse in consensual adolescent relationships and urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise judicial response instead of confusing it with a change in the statutory age.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Supreme Court’s decision concerning a Calcutta High Court ruling on adolescent relationships, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling.
2. The Supreme Court excluded consensual adolescent relationships from the operation of POCSO.
3. The Supreme Court used Article 142 for sentencing flexibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false: the Supreme Court set aside the ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO; it did not itself create such an exclusion.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed judicial holding as the false statement trap.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: POCSO Act — law applicable only to female children
POCSO Act — separate special law retained after replacement of the IPC by the BNS
POCSO Act — subsumed entirely into the BNS from 1 July 2024
POCSO Act — law dealing exclusively with child labour
accepted.x: The IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish repeal or replacement of the IPC from the continued existence of a separate special statute.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The age of consent under POCSO should not be confused with the legal age of marriage, which is:
o: 18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
16 years for women and 18 years for men
accepted.x: The age of consent under POCSO is 18 years. The legal marriage age referred to here is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
accepted.tq: Separate two closely related but legally distinct age thresholds.
accepted.sec: POCSO Act 2012 - full form, commencement, age, offences, special courts, 2019 amendment, age-of-consent debate  [APPSC]
